site.tagline: Morocco, with time for what matters to you.
site.hero_copy: A morning in the medina, a road through the Atlas, an evening beside the dunes. Discover Morocco with a little more time for the things you love.
site.collection_copy: Follow the coast, spend a night in the Sahara or step away from the city for the day. Find a journey that speaks to you, and we’ll help you make it your own.
site.about_title: A lovely trip begins with a conversation.
site.about_copy: Perhaps you have a route in mind. Perhaps it’s a desert evening, a beautiful riad or simply a change of scene. Tell us what draws you to Morocco, and we’ll take it from there.

sahara-marrakech-3-days.title: Three Days to the Sahara
sahara-marrakech-3-days.summary: Mountain passes, earthen kasbahs and an evening beside the dunes of Erg Chebbi. Three days from Marrakech for those who have always wanted to see the Sahara.
sahara-marrakech-3-days.story:
The road south is part of the pleasure: the folds of the High Atlas, the warm earth of Aït Ben Haddou and the tall walls of Todra Gorge. By the second evening, the landscape opens into dunes and the pace finally slows.

Spend a night near Erg Chebbi before the long road back to Marrakech. This is a full three days, with plenty of time on the road. If you can spare two more, our slower Sahara route gives you a whole day to enjoy the desert.
sahara-marrakech-3-days.fit: A short stay in Marrakech with the Sahara high on your wish list. You’ll need to be comfortable with long drives, particularly on the final day.
sahara-marrakech-3-days.practical: The return usually involves around 9–10 hours of driving, plus longer stops. Leave that evening free and avoid a flight connection on the same day. We’ll agree your camp facilities and camel or 4×4 transfer before booking.
steps: Leave Marrakech early and climb into the High Atlas. Explore Aït Ben Haddou, then continue through the Ouarzazate region and Valley of Roses to a guesthouse in the Dades Valley.
Stretch your legs beneath the cliffs of Todra Gorge before continuing east. Arrive at Erg Chebbi as the light changes across the dunes, with the evening to settle into camp.
Set off early for Marrakech, watching the landscapes of southern Morocco unfold again on the return. This is the longest day on the road, so keep your evening unhurried.

imperial-cities-sahara-9-days.title: Imperial Cities & Sahara Nights
imperial-cities-sahara-9-days.summary: From the courtyards of Fes to the dunes of Erg Chebbi, discover Morocco’s cities and southern landscapes on a nine-day journey from Casablanca to Marrakech.
imperial-cities-sahara-9-days.story:
Begin among the streets and monuments of Morocco’s imperial cities, where a doorway or a small workshop can be as absorbing as a famous landmark. A full day in Fes leaves time to explore its workshops, courtyards and neighborhoods in depth.

Then travel south through mountain country and the Ziz Valley for an evening in the Sahara. Kasbahs and the High Atlas lead you on to Marrakech, with another full day to explore before you leave.
imperial-cities-sahara-9-days.fit: A first visit with a love of history, architecture and changing scenery. Full days in Fes and Marrakech give you time to settle into each city.
imperial-cities-sahara-9-days.practical: The drives from Fes toward the desert and from Dades to Marrakech take much of the day. Monument and mosque visits follow local opening rules. An extra desert night is an option if you’d like a gentler pace.
steps: Meet in Casablanca and continue to Rabat. If your arrival time allows, enjoy a first look around Casablanca before heading to the capital.
Spend time in Rabat before continuing through Meknes and the Roman remains at Volubilis. Arrive in Fes for the night.
Explore Fes on foot, moving between historic buildings, working craft shops and the everyday life of the medina.
Cross the Middle Atlas and follow the Ziz Valley toward Erfoud, where the scenery begins to take on the colors of the desert.
Travel through the Tafilalt region to Merzouga. Reach the Erg Chebbi dunes for an evening at camp.
Leave the dunes behind and pause in Todra Gorge on the way to your next night in the Dades Valley.
Visit Aït Ben Haddou before crossing the High Atlas, arriving in Marrakech on the other side of the mountains.
Spend the day among gardens, historic courtyards and souks, with room to follow the parts of Marrakech that interest you most.
Enjoy your last moments in Morocco before a transfer arranged around your flight or onward plans.

slow-sahara-5-days.title: The Sahara, a Little Slower
slow-sahara-5-days.summary: Two nights near Merzouga and a whole day with the dunes. Take five days from Marrakech to enjoy the Sahara, the southern valleys and the places in between.
slow-sahara-5-days.story:
The first evening in the desert is only the beginning. With two nights near Erg Chebbi, there’s time to visit Khamlia, explore the surrounding settlements or simply watch the light move across the sand.

The journey home follows the Draa Valley, with a night near Ouarzazate before the Atlas crossing. Choose a camp, a lodge or a night in each—the right combination depends on how you like to spend your evenings.
slow-sahara-5-days.fit: Couples, photographers and anyone who would rather linger in the desert. The extra day gives the journey more breathing room, though there are still long drives.
slow-sahara-5-days.practical: The first and fourth days cover considerable distances. Your two desert nights can be in a camp, a lodge or a combination of both; we’ll set out the options before you book.
steps: Cross the Atlas and walk through Aït Ben Haddou before continuing into the southern valleys. Spend your first night in Dades.
Pause beneath the cliffs of Todra Gorge, then head east to Erg Chebbi for your first evening near the dunes.
Explore Khamlia and nearby oasis settlements, or leave the afternoon free to enjoy the dunes. A second night in the region means there’s no need to pack up just yet.
Travel through Rissani and the Draa Valley, breaking the return journey with a night near Ouarzazate.
Follow the road over the High Atlas, with stops at viewpoints as conditions allow, before returning to Marrakech.

marrakech-fes-sahara-4-days.title: Marrakech to Fes, via the Sahara
marrakech-fes-sahara-4-days.summary: Let the journey between two great medinas take you through kasbahs, gorges and the Sahara. Four days, with two nights near Merzouga and a full day around the dunes.
marrakech-fes-sahara-4-days.story:
Leave Marrakech across the Atlas and spend the first night in Dades. Beyond Todra Gorge, the road leads toward Merzouga and the broad sands of Erg Chebbi.

Two nights in the desert region leave a day for Khamlia, nearby settlements and quiet time at the dunes. Then follow the Ziz Valley and Middle Atlas north to Fes, arriving somewhere entirely different from where you began.
marrakech-fes-sahara-4-days.fit: A natural choice if you’re continuing from Marrakech to Fes and want to see the Sahara along the way. The route can also be requested in reverse.
marrakech-fes-sahara-4-days.practical: The first and final days involve long drives. Keep your arrival evening in Fes flexible, and allow extra time before any onward flight.
steps: Cross Tizi n’Tichka and visit Aït Ben Haddou before continuing through kasbah country to the Dades Valley for the night.
Travel through Todra Gorge to the dunes of Erg Chebbi. Your camp transfer will be arranged by camel or 4×4, according to your preference and confirmed plans.
Visit Khamlia and the surrounding desert region, with time to return to the dunes. Spend a second night near Merzouga.
Follow the Ziz Valley north through Midelt and the Middle Atlas. Reach Fes in the evening, ready for the next part of your stay.

southern-morocco-7-days.title: A Week in Southern Morocco
southern-morocco-7-days.summary: Stay among kasbahs, palm groves and valley landscapes before reaching the Sahara. A week from Marrakech with two nights near the dunes and time for the road south.
southern-morocco-7-days.story:
An evening near Aït Ben Haddou, palms around Skoura, the changing shapes of the Dades Valley: this journey gives the approach to the Sahara its own time and attention.

Near Merzouga, two nights make space for village visits, dune walks and a quieter afternoon. The return is broken near Ouarzazate, so the final Atlas crossing has a day of its own.
southern-morocco-7-days.fit: For those drawn to landscapes, small settlements and the south’s earthen architecture. A gradual approach to the Sahara with fewer city changes.
southern-morocco-7-days.practical: The route spreads the approach over several nights. Your proposal will include the selected stays, kasbah visits, camp arrangements and driving estimates.
steps: Take your time crossing the High Atlas and stay near Aït Ben Haddou, with its earthen buildings rising above the valley.
Continue through Ouarzazate to Skoura, where palm groves bring a welcome change of scenery.
Follow the Valley of Roses toward Dades and settle in for the night among the southern valleys.
Pause in Todra Gorge before continuing east to the dunes of Erg Chebbi.
Choose village visits or a walk among the dunes, or enjoy a quiet day at your accommodation.
Return through the southern valleys, stopping for the night near Ouarzazate.
Cross the High Atlas back to Marrakech, with pauses along the mountain road.

coast-desert-8-days.title: From the Sahara to Essaouira
coast-desert-8-days.summary: An evening by the dunes, a road through southern Morocco and two nights beside the Atlantic. Eight days of desert and coast, beginning and ending in Marrakech.
coast-desert-8-days.story:
Travel through the Atlas and Todra Gorge to a Sahara overnight, then turn west through Ouarzazate and Taroudant. By Essaouira, mountain roads have given way to sea air and fishing boats.

Two nights on the coast leave a full day for the medina, ramparts and a long lunch near the port. There’s a good deal of ground to cover between these landscapes; the reward is seeing how different one part of Morocco feels from the next.
coast-desert-8-days.fit: For travelers who want both desert and coast and enjoy a changing view from the road. Several days involve substantial driving.
coast-desert-8-days.practical: This route connects distant regions. If you prefer shorter drives, we can focus on either the Sahara or the coast and spend more time there.
steps: Cross the High Atlas and visit Aït Ben Haddou on the way to your first night in the Dades Valley.
Spend time in Todra Gorge, then continue toward Merzouga for an evening and overnight near the dunes.
Travel back through southern settlements and stop in Ouarzazate for the night.
Head west to Taroudant and spend the night around this walled southern city.
Continue toward the Atlantic and arrive in Essaouira for the first of two nights by the coast.
Wander the medina and ramparts, watch the fishing port at work or ask us to arrange a coastal activity.
Return through argan country to Marrakech, where you’ll spend your final night.
Enjoy a last walk if time allows, then continue to your flight or onward journey.

north-sahara-10-days.title: Tangier to Marrakech: Cities & Sahara
north-sahara-10-days.summary: From Tangier and Chefchaouen to Fes, the Sahara and Marrakech. Ten days following Morocco south, with time in the medinas and a full day near the dunes.
north-sahara-10-days.story:
Begin beside the Strait in Tangier before spending a night among Chefchaouen’s blue lanes. In Fes, a full day brings you closer to the workshops, courtyards and neighborhoods within the medina.

The route then turns south through the Ziz Valley to Merzouga. A desert day, Todra Gorge and the High Atlas lead you onward to Marrakech, without doubling back to your starting point.
north-sahara-10-days.fit: For a north-to-south holiday that brings together Chefchaouen, Fes and the Sahara. Particularly convenient when arriving in Tangier and leaving from Marrakech.
north-sahara-10-days.practical: Fes to Merzouga is a full day on the road. If you have more time, an overnight near Midelt can divide that drive and make the journey gentler.
steps: Arrive in Tangier, settle into your accommodation and enjoy a first look around the city as time allows.
Travel into the Rif Mountains and spend the night in Chefchaouen, with its blue streets and hillside setting.
Continue south to Fes. A visit to Volubilis can be considered if the day’s timing allows.
Explore the medina on foot, leaving time for the craft and architecture that catch your attention.
Make the long drive south through the Middle Atlas and Ziz Valley toward Merzouga.
Spend the day among the dunes and nearby communities, with a second evening in the desert region.
Leave Merzouga and travel through Todra Gorge toward the Dades Valley.
Visit Aït Ben Haddou and cross the High Atlas into Marrakech.
Choose a medina walk, time in the gardens or a day exploring on your own.
Leave for your flight or onward journey, with the transfer arranged around your plans.

grand-morocco-14-days.title: Two Weeks Through Morocco
grand-morocco-14-days.summary: Blue streets in the Rif, the medina of Fes, Sahara dunes and Atlantic mornings. Two weeks connecting Morocco’s cities and landscapes, with longer stays along the way.
grand-morocco-14-days.story:
There’s time here to see the country change: from Rabat and Chefchaouen to Fes, then through the mountains toward the Sahara. Full days in several stops let you do more than arrive, look around and leave.

After the desert and southern valleys, Marrakech brings gardens and lively souks. The journey finishes with Essaouira’s sea air before the return to Marrakech. It’s a wide-ranging first visit, with room to add a night wherever you’d like to linger.
grand-morocco-14-days.fit: A first Morocco visit with two weeks to explore and an appetite for variety. Expect a substantial road journey, balanced by longer stays in several destinations.
grand-morocco-14-days.practical: There are long driving days within this circuit. We’ll plan the final Essaouira-to-Marrakech transfer around your flight; an extra night in Marrakech is sensible for an early departure.
steps: Arrive in Casablanca and continue to Rabat, with any sightseeing arranged around your flight time.
Travel north into the Rif and settle into Chefchaouen.
Enjoy a full day among blue lanes, small squares and hillside viewpoints.
Continue to Fes, with a possible stop at Volubilis if the schedule allows.
Discover the medina’s craft workshops, courtyards and food on foot.
Cross the Middle Atlas and follow the Ziz Valley toward Merzouga and the Sahara.
Explore the desert region at your own pace and spend a second night near Erg Chebbi.
Leave the dunes for Todra Gorge and an overnight in the Dades Valley.
Visit Aït Ben Haddou before crossing the High Atlas to Marrakech.
Spend a day exploring Marrakech’s medina and gardens.
Try a cooking class, visit a hammam or leave the day free to follow your own interests.
Travel to Essaouira and settle into the slower rhythm of the coast.
Explore the fishing port, walk the ramparts and browse the medina’s artisan streets.
Return to Marrakech with ample time for your departure. For an early flight, add a final night in the city.

ouzoud-waterfalls.title: A Day at Ouzoud Waterfalls
ouzoud-waterfalls.summary: Follow shaded paths through olive groves, pause above the cascades and enjoy lunch with the sound of falling water. A full day in the countryside from Marrakech, with transport arranged for your group.
ouzoud-waterfalls.story:
The sound of the falls reaches you before the view opens. Paths weave between fig and olive trees, revealing different angles on the cascades as you make your way into the gorge.

With four to five hours in the area, there’s time for the walk, a riverside lunch and an optional boat ride near the spray. The day unfolds at a comfortable pace, with room to stop and enjoy the surroundings.
ouzoud-waterfalls.fit: A day outdoors for couples, families and friends who enjoy scenery and walking. The route can be adapted, though some paths are steep and uneven.
ouzoud-waterfalls.practical: Ouzoud is around 150 km from Marrakech, usually 2½–3 hours each way. Wear shoes with good grip: paths can be slippery, and the climb back takes 20–30 minutes. Swimming and boat trips depend on conditions. Watch the macaques from a distance and avoid feeding them.
itinerary: 08:30 · Set off from Marrakech
Your driver meets you at your accommodation or the nearest accessible meeting point. Settle in for the drive northeast, leaving the bustle of Marrakech behind.
Morning · Through the Tadla plains
Farmland and olive groves fill the view as you approach the Middle Atlas foothills. The journey takes around three hours, with a stop along the way to stretch your legs.
Around 11:30 · First views of Ouzoud
Arrive in Tanaghmeilt village and take in the waterfalls. Choose the walking route that suits you before beginning the descent into the gorge.
Late morning & afternoon · Beside the falls
Spend around four to five hours exploring, including time for lunch. Follow shaded paths between viewpoints, look for macaques in the trees and, if you wish, take a boat closer to the spray.
Lunch · A table by the cascades
Choose a café overlooking the water for a Moroccan lunch, or find a place to enjoy your picnic. Lunch, drinks and the optional boat ride are payable separately unless included in your quote.
Before 16:00 · Back through the village
Allow 20–30 minutes for the walk uphill, with a little time to browse the village stalls before meeting your driver.
Around 16:00 · The road home
Relax on the drive back, with a break along the way. You’ll reach your accommodation in Marrakech between 19:00 and 20:00, depending on traffic.
cover: Your own driver and comfortable, air-conditioned transport
Collection and return at your accommodation or a nearby accessible point
The agreed schedule, rest stops and time at the falls
A clear breakdown of lunch and optional boat arrangements
ouzoud-waterfalls.extras: Lunch, drinks, the optional boat ride, shopping and tips are separate unless included in your proposal. We’ll agree the final arrangements and cancellation terms with you before booking.

ourika-valley.title: A Day in the Ourika Valley
ourika-valley.summary: Walnut trees, hillside villages and lunch beside the river. Leave Marrakech for the Ourika Valley, with a waterfall walk at Setti Fatma or a quieter afternoon by the water.
ourika-valley.story:
As the road follows the river into the Atlas foothills, Marrakech begins to feel a world away. Terraced fields and villages line the valley, and the cafés at Setti Fatma invite you to stay for lunch.

Walk up to the first waterfall if you’d like a more active day, or keep to the village and riverbank. Either way, there’s time to enjoy the scenery without hurrying from one stop to the next.
ourika-valley.fit: For a change of scene close to Marrakech. Choose the waterfall trail for a more active outing, or spend your time in the village and beside the river.
ourika-valley.practical: The waterfall trail is rocky and can be steep or slippery, so walking shoes are essential. Staying by the river is the gentler option; let us know which you prefer when planning your day.
itinerary: 09:00 · Leave Marrakech behind
Your driver meets you at your accommodation or a nearby accessible point. Head south toward the Atlas foothills as the city gives way to open countryside.
On the way · Meet the argan producers
Stop at a women’s cooperative to see how argan oil is made. There’s time to look around and browse the products if something catches your eye.
Around 10:00 · Along the Ourika River
Follow the valley past walnut trees, terraced fields and villages on the slopes. On Mondays, stop at Tnin Ourika’s weekly market for a glimpse of local life.
Setti Fatma · Waterfall or riverbank
Take the rocky path to the first waterfall, allowing around 45 minutes in each direction. Or stay in the village, explore its cafés and enjoy the river. We’ll arrange the day around your choice.
Lunch · Under the trees
Find a table beside the river for tagine or grilled dishes, with the water flowing nearby. Lunch and drinks are payable separately unless included in your quote.
Afternoon · A little time to linger
Browse the craft stalls or settle by the water. If you’d like to cool off in the river pools, check the local conditions first.
17:00–18:00 · Return to Marrakech
Enjoy the views on the drive back down the valley. Your driver brings you to your accommodation or the return point agreed for the day.

essaouira-day.title: Essaouira, a Day by the Sea
essaouira-day.summary: Blue fishing boats, sea-facing ramparts and a medina made for wandering. Spend a day on the Atlantic coast, with time for a seafood lunch and a walk along the shore.
essaouira-day.story:
Essaouira feels different from the moment you arrive: cooler air, gulls over the harbor and the Atlantic just beyond the medina walls. Walk between small workshops and galleries, then follow the boats to the fishing port.

The afternoon is yours to enjoy. Find a table for lunch, browse the souks or pause for mint tea on Place Moulay Hassan. Your driver takes care of the return to Marrakech; if a single day feels too short, ask us about staying overnight.
essaouira-day.fit: For a taste of the coast during a Marrakech stay. There are roughly three hours of travel each way, with around four hours to enjoy Essaouira.
essaouira-day.practical: Allow around three hours each way, depending on traffic and stops. Bring a layer for the Atlantic breeze. A medina visit can be arranged, and an overnight stay is an option if you’d like more time.
itinerary: 08:30 · Toward the Atlantic
Meet your driver at your accommodation and head west across the Haouz plains. The coast is your destination today, with a few pauses along the way.
Morning · Coffee & argan country
Stop for coffee in Chichaoua, then visit a women’s cooperative to see the traditional extraction of argan oil. Continue through the argan-growing countryside toward the sea.
Around 12:00 · Welcome to Essaouira
Arrive near the medina entrance, with around four hours to explore. Wander independently or follow a medina visit arranged in advance.
Midday · Inside the sea walls
Follow narrow lanes past workshops and galleries, then walk the Skala ramparts for views of the Atlantic. Look out for thuya woodwork and silver jewelry along the way.
Lunch · Down by the harbor
Stroll among the blue fishing boats before choosing lunch near the port or in the medina. Grilled seafood is a natural choice here. Lunch is payable separately unless included in your quote.
Afternoon · Your time on the coast
Walk along the sandy beach, return to a favorite shop or enjoy mint tea on Place Moulay Hassan. Leave a little time simply to sit and watch the town go by.
Around 16:00 · Back to Marrakech
Your driver meets you near the medina entrance for the journey inland. With breaks along the way, expect to reach your accommodation between 19:00 and 20:00.

ait-ben-haddou-day.title: Across the Atlas to Aït Ben Haddou
ait-ben-haddou-day.summary: Wind through the High Atlas to Aït Ben Haddou’s earthen towers and the kasbahs of Ouarzazate. A full day of mountain views, village lanes and Morocco’s film country.
ait-ben-haddou-day.story:
The Atlas crossing offers a changing view at every turn: hillside villages, cultivated terraces and peaks rising above the road. Beyond the pass, Aït Ben Haddou stands in warm earth against the valley.

Explore its lanes and climb toward the old granary before continuing to Ouarzazate and Taourirt Kasbah. Film lovers can add a visit to the Atlas studios. It’s a long day, but a striking introduction to the landscapes south of Marrakech.
ait-ben-haddou-day.fit: For travelers drawn to architecture, film locations and mountain scenery, with a full day free and a liking for a scenic drive.
ait-ben-haddou-day.practical: Expect an early start, an evening return and winding mountain roads. Comfortable shoes are best for the uneven lanes and uphill walk. Monument tickets, meals and any local assistance will be detailed in your quote; the film studios are optional. Weather and road conditions may affect the schedule.
itinerary: Around 07:00 · Into the High Atlas
Your driver meets you at your accommodation for an early departure. Climb into the mountains past terraced hillsides and villages overlooking the road.
Morning · Tizi n’Tichka
Pause at viewpoints around the 2,260-metre pass. Take in the peaks and the road winding below before descending toward the southern kasbahs.
Midday · The lanes of Aït Ben Haddou
Explore the fortified village on foot, following earthen lanes toward the granary at the top. Enjoy the valley views and look for settings you may recognize from film and television.
Afternoon · Ouarzazate & its film studios
Continue to Ouarzazate and Taourirt Kasbah. If you’ve chosen to visit the Atlas Film Studios, explore the sets along the way. Studio admission is an optional extra.
Lunch · A pause in Ouarzazate
Take a seat at a local restaurant for tagine, couscous or grilled dishes. Lunch and drinks are payable separately unless included in your quote.
Afternoon · The mountain road home
Cross the Atlas once more, with a different light on the slopes. A stop at an argan cooperative can be added on request if time allows.
Around 19:00 · Back in Marrakech
Return to your accommodation or agreed meeting point, with the evening ahead after a full day in the mountains.

agafay-evening.title: An Evening in Agafay
agafay-evening.summary: Watch the light soften over Agafay’s rocky hills, then settle in for an evening meal. Open skies and desert scenery, within an evening’s reach of Marrakech.
agafay-evening.story:
Beyond Marrakech, the stone desert opens into low hills and a wide horizon. Arrive with time to take in the late-afternoon light before dinner at your chosen venue.

You can keep the evening simple—a view, a meal and time together—or add a camel ride or quad outing. We’ll help you choose the setting and agree the details before you go.
agafay-evening.fit: An easy change of scene for a free evening in Marrakech, especially if you’d like desert landscapes without a multi-day journey.
agafay-evening.practical: Agafay is a rocky desert, distinct from the Sahara’s sand dunes. Your venue, menu, drinks, optional activities and return time are agreed before booking.
steps: Leave Marrakech for your chosen venue in Agafay. Arrive with time to settle in and enjoy the open landscape.
Find a viewpoint as the light changes across the hills, or enjoy a camel or quad session arranged separately.
Sit down to dinner at the selected venue, then return to Marrakech at the agreed time.

imlil-atlas-day.title: Imlil & the Atlas, by Way of Agafay
imlil-atlas-day.summary: Rocky desert, lake views and a walk among mountain villages. Follow the road from Agafay through Lalla Takerkoust and the Kik Plateau to Imlil, with a camel ride and lunch along the way.
imlil-atlas-day.story:
See the landscapes around Marrakech change in a single day: Agafay’s stony hills, the water at Lalla Takerkoust and the terraces below the Kik Plateau. A camel ride and tea with a Berber family bring time to pause between the views.

In Imlil, leave the road for a walk through the mountain villages. Paths lead past walnut trees, hamlets and streams before lunch in a Berber home. The return follows Moulay Brahim Gorge back toward Marrakech.
imlil-atlas-day.fit: For travelers who enjoy a varied day outdoors, with a one- to two-hour mountain walk. We’ll plan the trail and camel ride around your group’s comfort.
imlil-atlas-day.practical: This is a sightseeing circuit with a one- to two-hour walk, rather than a Toubkal summit trek. Bring walking shoes, sun protection and a warm layer. The Asni market stop is on Saturdays. Your quote will detail the camel ride, local assistance and home-hosted lunch; weather, traffic and walking pace can affect the return time.
itinerary: 09:00 · From Marrakech to Agafay
Your driver meets you for the day’s journey by 4×4. Head southwest, stopping to take in the views as farmland gives way to Agafay’s rocky hills.
Morning · A camel ride in Agafay
Join the camel team for an hour among stony hills and dry valleys, with the Atlas Mountains stretching across the horizon.
Lalla Takerkoust · Beside the lake
Pause by the water for photographs and a quiet moment before the road begins to climb.
Kik Plateau · Mountain views & mint tea
Look out over terraces and hillside settlements, then visit a Berber family for mint tea and homemade bread. On Saturdays, the route also takes in Asni’s weekly market.
Afternoon · On foot around Imlil
Begin a one- to two-hour walk through walnut terraces, hamlets and streams toward the waterfalls. The pace is set to suit your group.
Lunch · At a Berber home
Enjoy a three-course Moroccan lunch in Imlil with views over the valley: salad, tagine or couscous, followed by fruit and mint tea.
By 17:00 · Home through the gorge
Return through Moulay Brahim Gorge and the Asni area. The drive takes around an hour and a half, bringing you back to Marrakech for the evening.

chefchaouen-from-fes.title: Chefchaouen from Fes
chefchaouen-from-fes.summary: Blue-painted lanes, small squares and the Rif Mountains beyond. Travel from Fes for a day in Chefchaouen, with time to walk, stop for lunch and enjoy the views.
chefchaouen-from-fes.story:
The road from Fes leads north toward the Rif and the hillside town of Chefchaouen. Once there, narrow blue lanes and small squares invite a slower kind of exploring.

Spend the middle of the day on foot, pausing for lunch and photographs before the return. If you’d like to enjoy the town after the day visitors leave, we can discuss an overnight stay instead.
chefchaouen-from-fes.fit: For travelers based in Fes with a full day available. An overnight stay gives you more time in town and a gentler pace.
chefchaouen-from-fes.practical: This excursion starts in Fes. The return drive takes a large part of the day, so keep your evening flexible. A one-way finish and overnight stay can be arranged on request.
steps: Leave Fes early from the meeting point agreed near your riad and travel north toward the Rif Mountains.
Explore the blue medina on foot, with time for photographs, small squares and lunch at a place that takes your fancy.
Meet your driver for the return to Fes, or continue your stay in Chefchaouen if you’ve arranged a one-way journey.

volubilis-meknes.title: Volubilis, Moulay Idriss & Meknes
volubilis-meknes.summary: Roman remains, a hillside town and an imperial city. Discover three chapters of Morocco’s history on a day out from Fes.
volubilis-meknes.story:
Begin among the open-air remains of Volubilis, where walking through the site gives a sense of the city that once stood here. Nearby Moulay Idriss brings a different setting, with a short visit and time for lunch.

Continue to Meknes for the afternoon before returning to Fes. The day’s monument visits follow current access arrangements, leaving room to enjoy the places that are open.
volubilis-meknes.fit: For travelers staying in Fes who enjoy archaeology, history and architecture. Expect walking at exposed sites and a varied day of visits.
volubilis-meknes.practical: Bring sun protection for Volubilis, where there is little shade. Some monuments in Meknes may be affected by restoration; we’ll confirm the available visits before departure.
steps: Travel from Fes to Volubilis and explore the Roman site. A local introduction to its history can be arranged if you’d like more context.
Continue to nearby Moulay Idriss for a short visit and a pause for lunch.
Discover the accessible landmarks of Meknes before returning to Fes at the end of the day.

marrakech-balloon.title: A Morning Above Marrakech
marrakech-balloon.summary: Leave before sunrise for a balloon flight over the countryside around Marrakech. A different view of Morocco, with the Atlas on the distant horizon.
marrakech-balloon.story:
An early start brings you to the launch area while the day is still beginning. After the briefing and preparations, take to the sky when conditions allow and watch the countryside spread out below.

The flight is one part of the morning, with breakfast and transfers arranged according to your chosen session. Leave the rest of the morning open so there’s no need to rush after landing.
marrakech-balloon.fit: For an early riser looking for a different view of the Marrakech countryside, with a morning free and flexibility if the weather changes.
marrakech-balloon.practical: Flights depend on suitable weather and the operator’s eligibility rules. Your booking details will set out the flight duration and the options for cancellation or rescheduling.
steps: Travel to the launch area before sunrise and meet the team for your briefing and the morning’s preparations.
Take to the sky when conditions permit. The operator will confirm the flight time, which is shorter than the complete morning outing.
Enjoy the breakfast and return arrangements included in your chosen session, then head back to Marrakech.

agafay-quad.title: Quad Riding in Agafay
agafay-quad.summary: Leave the city for Agafay’s open tracks and rocky hills. Get familiar with the quad, then follow the lead vehicle through the landscape with time for scenic stops.
agafay-quad.story:
Agafay’s terrain gives this outing its character: stony tracks, low hills and long views. A briefing and practice session at the base help you settle in before the ride begins.

Follow the lead vehicle along the agreed route, pausing to take in the scenery. We’ll make the time on the trail, transfers and driver or passenger arrangements clear when planning your outing.
agafay-quad.fit: For an active break from Marrakech, whether you’re interested in driving or joining as a passenger. Eligibility and the riding setup are agreed in advance.
agafay-quad.practical: Check the minimum driving age, license requirements and insurance cover before booking. The total outing includes transfers and preparation as well as the ride itself.
steps: Travel to the activity base, collect your helmet and learn the controls with instructions and a practice session.
Follow the lead vehicle through the rocky landscape, with pauses to enjoy the views along the agreed route.
Finish the ride at the base and meet your driver for the journey back.

merzouga-camel.title: A Camel Ride Among the Dunes
merzouga-camel.summary: See Erg Chebbi from camelback as the dunes change color around you. A short outing from Merzouga, with sunrise or sunset options and time to pause along the way.
merzouga-camel.story:
A camel’s measured pace gives you time to look around: the shape of the dunes, the changing light and the space beyond the next ridge. Follow a short route from Merzouga before returning to your starting point.

Choose the time that suits your stay and comfort. A 4×4 alternative can be discussed if camel riding isn’t for you, and a camp night can be arranged separately.
merzouga-camel.fit: For travelers already in Merzouga who would like a short dune outing. Overnight camping and transport from other cities are separate arrangements.
merzouga-camel.practical: This activity starts in Merzouga and does not include transport from Marrakech. Camel riding involves uneven movement; ask about a 4×4 alternative if that would be more comfortable.
steps: Meet at the agreed point in Merzouga and receive an introduction before setting off.
Follow a short route through the dunes, with pauses to enjoy the views and take photographs.
Return to the starting point. If you’d like to stay overnight at a camp, we can arrange that separately.

merzouga-sandboarding.title: Sandboarding at Erg Chebbi
merzouga-sandboarding.summary: A board, a dune and another reason to spend time outside. Try sandboarding near Merzouga, with space to practice and enjoy the views between runs.
merzouga-sandboarding.story:
Add a little play to a desert stay. Start on a suitable dune, learn the basics and find your own rhythm, with time to rest between the climbs back up.

The session is planned around the heat and wind. It works well as a local activity while staying in Merzouga; transfers and overnight camp stays are separate arrangements.
merzouga-sandboarding.fit: For travelers already in Merzouga who enjoy being active outdoors and are comfortable walking uphill through sand.
merzouga-sandboarding.practical: You’ll walk back up the dune between runs. The time and location depend on heat and wind conditions. Equipment, meeting arrangements and any transport will be confirmed before the session.
steps: Meet locally, collect your board and agree on a dune suited to the day’s conditions.
Learn the basics and try the slope, taking a breather between climbs and enjoying the surrounding dunes.
Return your equipment and continue the rest of your day in Merzouga.

agafay-buggy.title: Agafay by Buggy
agafay-buggy.summary: Take to Agafay’s rocky tracks on a buggy drive. Open views, a little adventure and time to get comfortable at the wheel before you begin.
agafay-buggy.story:
Meet at the base, learn the controls and settle into your seat before following the lead vehicle into Agafay’s open landscape. Scenic pauses give you time to look beyond the trail.

The route responds to conditions on the day. We’ll clarify who’s driving, who’s joining as a passenger and how much time you’ll spend on the trail, alongside the transfers and preparation.
agafay-buggy.fit: For an outdoor driving experience near Marrakech, including friends or couples who would like to share a buggy. Capacity and eligibility depend on the vehicle and operator.
agafay-buggy.practical: Age and license rules, helmets, insurance and seats per buggy must be agreed before booking. The driving session is shorter than the complete outing.
steps: Arrive at the base, agree driver and passenger roles and get familiar with the controls during the briefing.
Follow the lead vehicle on a circuit through the rocky hills, with stops to enjoy the scenery.
Return to the base and meet your driver for the journey to Marrakech.

atlas-paragliding.title: Above the Atlas Foothills
atlas-paragliding.summary: See the foothills from the air on a tandem flight with a pilot. A striking change of perspective near Marrakech, planned around the day’s flying conditions.
atlas-paragliding.story:
From the launch site, the landscape takes on a different scale. Meet your pilot, prepare together and take off only when the weather and site conditions are suitable.

Keep your schedule flexible for this outing. The launch location and flight time depend on conditions, and we’ll clarify the operator’s arrangements, eligibility and weather policy before booking.
atlas-paragliding.fit: For travelers curious about tandem flying who can leave room for weather changes in their plans.
atlas-paragliding.practical: The operator’s qualifications, insurance, eligibility rules and weather cancellation terms must be verified before booking. A particular launch site or flight duration cannot be guaranteed.
steps: Travel to the selected site and meet the operator to review conditions and eligibility for the flight.
Prepare with your tandem pilot and follow the briefing. The flight goes ahead only when conditions allow.
Meet your return transport at the landing site and travel back to Marrakech.

marrakech-hammam.title: Time for a Hammam
marrakech-hammam.summary: A welcome pause between days of exploring Marrakech. Choose a traditional bathhouse or a spa setting and make time for Morocco’s bathing ritual.
marrakech-hammam.story:
After hours on your feet in the medina, a hammam offers a different way to spend part of the day. Warmth, water and a slower pace make the visit as much about taking time as the treatment itself.

A neighborhood bathhouse and a spa are different experiences. We’ll discuss the setting, privacy and treatments with you, so you know what to expect and can choose what feels comfortable.
marrakech-hammam.fit: For a quiet break during a Marrakech stay. Tell us the setting and level of privacy you’d prefer, from a traditional bathhouse to a spa.
marrakech-hammam.practical: Privacy, treatment length and what to bring vary by venue. A massage may be available as an extra; it is not automatically part of the hammam session.
steps: Choose between a traditional bathhouse and a spa, with privacy and treatments agreed before your visit.
Your host takes you through the treatment you’ve chosen, with time to settle into the experience.
Leave a little space in your day afterward, rather than heading straight to the next activity.

marrakech-cooking.title: A Moroccan Kitchen in Marrakech
marrakech-cooking.summary: Learn a few of the flavors you’ve been enjoying, then sit down to the meal you’ve made. A hands-on cooking class, with a market visit available for selected sessions.
marrakech-cooking.story:
There’s something satisfying about learning a dish in the place it comes from. Work through a Moroccan menu with your host, ask questions as you cook and pick up ideas to bring home.

Some classes begin with a market visit; others take you straight to the kitchen. The session ends around the table, enjoying the food together. We’ll agree the menu and dietary needs before you arrive.
marrakech-cooking.fit: For curious cooks, couples and families who enjoy learning by doing. Share any allergies, dietary preferences and your preferred language when planning the class.
marrakech-cooking.practical: Allergies and dietary needs should be shared before the menu is agreed. Market visits, teaching language and transport depend on the host and selected session.
steps: Meet your host for a market visit if arranged, or begin in the kitchen with an introduction to the ingredients.
Prepare a seasonal Moroccan menu with step-by-step guidance and time to ask questions along the way.
Enjoy the dishes you’ve prepared and note down the details you’d like to try in your own kitchen.

marrakech-dinner-show.title: Dinner & an Evening Show
marrakech-dinner-show.summary: Bring Moroccan food and an evening performance into your Marrakech stay. Choose a venue and program that suit the kind of night you have in mind.
marrakech-dinner-show.story:
Make an evening of it, with dinner and a performance in one setting. The atmosphere, menu and style of show vary by venue, so choosing the right one is part of the planning.

We’ll help clarify the program, drinks and transport before you decide. If you’re traveling with children or prefer an earlier finish, let us know so the evening works for everyone.
marrakech-dinner-show.fit: For friends, families or couples who would like an organized evening out. Your choice of venue determines the atmosphere and performance style.
marrakech-dinner-show.practical: Programs vary by venue and season. Review the menu and performance details, including any animal participation, before choosing. Drinks, upgrades and transfers should be clear in your quote.
steps: Meet at the chosen venue, or arrive with transport arranged for your evening.
Enjoy the agreed menu and performance. Drinks and any upgrades are detailed separately in your booking arrangements.
Return at the agreed time, with your transfer planned in advance if requested.

essaouira-horse-riding.title: Essaouira on Horseback
essaouira-horse-riding.summary: Leave the medina for a ride along the coast. Meet the stable team and follow a trail chosen for your experience, with sea air and open scenery along the way.
essaouira-horse-riding.story:
A ride outside Essaouira offers a different view of the coast, away from the harbor and busy streets. Begin at the stable, where the team will discuss your experience and introduce you to your horse.

The route and pace suit the riders and conditions. Beach access is not always possible, and a gallop is not part of every ride—the pleasure is in exploring the landscape on horseback.
essaouira-horse-riding.fit: For travelers staying in Essaouira who would like time in the saddle. Tell us about each rider’s experience so the stable can suggest a suitable horse and pace.
essaouira-horse-riding.practical: Confirm rider age and weight limits, helmets, insurance and stable standards before booking. Beach access depends on conditions. This is a local outing; any transfers are arranged separately.
steps: Meet the stable team, talk through your riding experience and receive a helmet and introductory instructions.
Follow the stable team along a suitable coastal trail at the agreed pace. The day’s conditions determine access to the beach.
Return to the stable and finish the outing locally, ready to enjoy the rest of your time in Essaouira.
